semantic_correction.stem: A nurse is performing a focused abdominal assessment on a client with new abdominal distention. Which action should the nurse take before palpating the abdomen?

options.A: Auscultate the abdomen for bowel sounds before palpation so the nurse assesses bowel activity before touch can alter the sounds being evaluated.
options.B: Palpate the area of greatest tenderness first so the most symptomatic region is assessed before the client becomes fatigued by the examination.
options.C: Ask the client to tighten the abdominal muscles before palpation so the abdominal wall is easier to evaluate and underlying structures are stabilized.
options.D: Palpate the abdominal quadrants rapidly before auscultation to stimulate peristalsis and make bowel sounds easier to hear during the remainder of the assessment.

semantic_correction.rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI/Open RN Nursing Skills guidance states that abdominal assessment differs from many other physical examinations because palpation should occur after auscultation of bowel sounds. Auscultation follows inspection and is performed before palpation so bowel sounds can be assessed accurately without mechanical stimulation altering bowel activity. Current StatPearls abdominal-examination guidance independently states that auscultation precedes palpation to avoid provoking or suppressing bowel activity through mechanical stimulation. Therefore the nurse should auscultate before palpating. B is incorrect because when abdominal pain is present, the tender area is generally assessed last rather than first. C is incorrect because voluntary abdominal-wall contraction interferes with palpation rather than improving it. D is incorrect because intentionally palpating first can alter bowel activity and reduce the accuracy of the subsequent bowel-sound assessment.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Perform focused abdominal assessment in the correct sequence by auscultating bowel sounds before palpation to avoid altering bowel activity and the sounds being assessed.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests abdominal-assessment sequence with one clearly best answer, balanced alternatives, current source verification, and no absolute-word cue.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches current guidance to auscultate before palpation so bowel sounds are not altered by mechanical stimulation.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Tender areas are generally palpated last to reduce discomfort and guarding.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Abdominal muscle contraction makes palpation more difficult and does not improve assessment accuracy.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Palpation before auscultation can alter bowel activity and compromise the bowel-sound assessment.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A uniquely follows the correct assessment sequence; B prioritizes tenderness incorrectly, C promotes muscle guarding, and D intentionally alters bowel activity before auscultation.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel abdominal-assessment actions of comparable length and specificity; the prior absolute-word distractor was removed.
